name: Megali Idea
summary: The Megali Idea (Great Idea) is the Greek irredentist programme of uniting the Greeks still outside the kingdom, in the Ottoman Empire and elsewhere, in one state centred on Constantinople. It joined a modern constitutional nation with the memory of classical Athens and the Orthodox Byzantine Empire. It guided Greek foreign policy from 1844 until the defeat in Asia Minor in 1922.
scope: The mainstream Greek irredentist programme from Kolettis's 1844 speech to the Venizelist drive at the Paris Peace Conference and the 1919-1922 Asia Minor war. Based on Kolettis's speech in the 1843-44 National Assembly, Venizelos's 1919 memorandum and standard historical accounts. It excludes later Greek or Cypriot nationalism after 1922 and the communist and royalist factions' separate agendas. Economic and social answers are mostly inferred and low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Pre-1922 Greek nationalism had no health programme; Venizelist liberalism leaned toward modest social reform, but adherents were not defined by it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Venizelos passed early labour laws, but wage floors were not part of the national project and adherents had no common line.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The idea was about borders, not economics; Venizelist liberals favoured a mixed, capitalist order while Kolettis-era politics was patronage-based.

public-ownership.rationale: Venizelism was bourgeois-liberal and never advocated nationalising industry; inferred from its liberal reform record.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No stated position; war finance and refugee settlement pressed on budgets but the ideology had no distributive doctrine.

unions-good.rationale: Venizelos legalised some labour organisation in 1910s reforms, yet the ideology treated class interests as secondary to the nation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Venizelist liberalism assumed a bourgeois property order; inferred, not stated in the idea itself.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Economic regulation was not part of the idea; adherents divided by party.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; the 19th-century kingdom had almost no welfare state to cut, so no clear position can be inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Alien to a nationalist-liberal programme; inferred from Venizelism's capitalist orientation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anachronistic question; security policy was subordinate to the national struggle but no stance on surveillance is documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the conservative, Orthodox-inflected social outlook of Greek nationalism.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents had no defined view.

strong-leader.rationale: Kolettis ruled through patronage and Venizelos was a charismatic leader, but the Venizelist cause was constitutional and fought royal overreach, so adherents split.

state-harmful.rationale: The idea is about building a larger Greek state with Constantinople as capital, so calling the state harmful is the opposite of its core aim.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; no documented position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Venizelos modernised the army before the Balkan Wars and the idea required military strength to realise it.

decide-locally.rationale: Kolettis and Venizelos built a centralised nation-state aiming to gather all Hellenes under one government in Athens or Constantinople.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy was not part of the idea.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox, conservative social setting in which the idea flourished; not a doctrinal element.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Orthodox-linked social conservatism of its adherents.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Orthodox Christian identity that Kolettis treated as binding the nation.

more-religion-public.rationale: Kolettis called religion the guardian of national unity and defined Greeks as those who believe in Christ, giving Orthodoxy a public national role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; the idea has no position on redress for racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from traditional social views of the period.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kolettis's speech and the idea itself rest on preserving and reuniting Hellenic and Byzantine heritage as the national mission.

gradual-change.rationale: The idea pursued sudden territorial transformation through war and revolt, and Venizelos staged a revolution in 1916, though within established monarchy early on.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Greek nationalism treated co-ethnics as returnees rather than immigrants; no stance on general immigration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Venizelos appealed to the Peace Conference and League principles, but adherents wanted Greek sovereignty, not supranational authority; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; adherents had no common trade doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: The memorandum asks that Greek national claims be met in the peace settlement and puts national unity ahead of other aims.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Greek claims were framed as liberating oppressed co-nationals, so intervention for kin is accepted, though the statement is broader.

open-borders.rationale: The project was to redraw borders around Greek populations, and Venizelos proposed population movements to homogenise states.

limit-growth.rationale: Anachronistic; the idea assumes expansion of state and population.

revolution-justified.rationale: The idea grew from the 1821 uprising and Greek revolts in Crete and Macedonia; Kolettis invokes the oath of the revolution as the nation's founding act.

experts-over-public.rationale: No stated position; Venizelos favoured technocratic reform yet the Venizelist base was mass-popular.

central-planning.rationale: Alien to its liberal-nationalist outlook; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism was not defined by the idea; no consistent doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Venizelos pursued state-led modernisation, but it was not a defining position of the idea.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Venizelos pursued land reform for small cultivators, inferred as a mild Venizelist leaning.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Incompatible with the bourgeois liberal nationalism of Venizelism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not an issue for the idea; inferred rejection of radical monetary views.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatism was not part of the idea; Venizelism was parliamentary-liberal.

one-party-rule.rationale: The idea was pursued through parliamentary and constitutional politics, and Venizelos fought a royalist-liberal electoral rivalry.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The idea began under King Otto and George I and most adherents supported a crowned Greek state, though the National Schism split Venizelists from the crown.

democracy-best.rationale: Kolettis demanded citizenship and constitutional rights for all Greeks, and Venizelism championed the 1911 constitution; democratic form was accepted rather than elevated.

direct-votes.rationale: Venizelism relied on parliamentary representation; direct democracy was not a theme.

workers-councils.rationale: Contrary to its liberal-nationalist, class-collaborationist framing.

right-to-secede.rationale: The idea is irredentist and unifying; it aims at the annexation of territories to Greece, not at regions leaving states.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; Greek nationalists claimed a civilisational mission but not a doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Its history includes armed revolts, guerrilla action in Macedonia and a war for Asia Minor, so adherents did not hold violence unjustified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Greeks accepted war as the means to realise the idea, but the sources do not frame war as character-building; adherents split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Kolettis fused national and Orthodox identity, defining Greeks as Christians and linking the Church to the national cause.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Orthodoxy shaped national identity but the idea sought a constitutional state, not scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A national state with a strong army was the vehicle of the idea.

military-superiority.rationale: Venizelos reformed the army to win over rivals; the idea required Greek forces strong enough to prevail over neighbours.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Venizelos's memorandum argues for borders by Greek population majorities and proposes migrations so that remaining states are homogeneous, though Kolettis defined Greeks by religion.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The nation, not class, was the driving unit of the idea.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not part of the idea; inferred from its liberal orientation.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic; Greek claims treated the land as historically Greek.

civilizational-union.rationale: The idea sought union of Greeks and Orthodox Christians, aiming to restore a Byzantine-style Orthodox centre.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The idea asks sacrifice for the nation, but it takes no stand on whether self-interest is moral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Kolettis stressed the oath and the sacrifices of the struggle as national duties, yet he also insisted on civil rights for all Greeks, so it is mild.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from nationalist wish to expand Greek demographic strength.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anachronistic; the idea sought modernisation and state growth.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Nothing in the sources links the idea to a view on technological speed.

restore-past-order.rationale: The idea aimed to restore a Byzantine-style Orthodox empire centred on Constantinople, a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Venizelos was pragmatic, but the idea itself is a doctrinal national programme; split.

direct-action.rationale: Politics ran through parliament and diplomacy as well as revolt; Venizelos used both, so action outside elections was not central.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources record no stance on whether methods should mirror intended ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Opposed to the state-building, civilizing aims of the idea.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not part of the idea; inferred rejection.

production-for-use.rationale: Not part of the idea; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Incompatible with its national-liberal programme; Venizelos opposed communism.

collective-farming.rationale: Venizelist agrarian policy favoured smallholders, not collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Greek nationalism saw wars as national liberation, not a capitalist product.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state seeking war and expansion required taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Not a theme of the idea.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The idea ascribes rights to the Hellenic nation as a collective that spans states, though Kolettis also stressed individual citizenship.

conscription.rationale: Venizelos reorganised and expanded compulsory military service and the Balkan Wars and Asia Minor campaign relied on mobilised conscripts.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The national project binds people to the state; exit as a check is alien.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a national and sacred vehicle, not a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: The idea was about national liberation, and none of the sources discusses material preconditions of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source ties the idea to a claim about media or university power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Kolettis used 'race' but defined Greeks by faith and history; no hereditarian claim.

organic-representation.rationale: Parliamentary representation, not organic corporatism, was the Venizelist framework.

total-state.rationale: A national liberal constitutional state is the vehicle; no ideology of directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Kolettis's speech presents Greece as a nation rising again after antiquity and Byzantium, completing a restoration.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Annexing Greek-populated and historically Greek lands is the defining aim of the idea.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Modern constitutional nationalism rejects lordly oaths as a basis for rule.

bound-labor.rationale: Rejected by a modern liberal state.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a classical-rationalist heritage.

universal-morality.rationale: Kolettis appeals to Hellenic heritage and Christianity, but no universal-moral doctrine is stated.

single-common-good.rationale: Kolettis stressed national unity over factional disputes, yet adherents were split along party lines.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Kolettis argued that Greeks born outside the kingdom held rights to citizenship in it, and the project aimed to gather diaspora Greeks into the state.

revive-national-language.rationale: Greek was already spoken; the question matches only loosely, since the Hellenic revival emphasised educated Greek language as a national tie.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Company governance was outside the idea, so adherents had no shared view.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education policy appears only as Hellenic cultural revival, not as a funding scheme.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal doctrine was no part of the idea; war finance was driven by national aims.

economic-freedom.rationale: The idea made no claim about economic and political freedom lasting together.

rule-by-example.rationale: The sources show no doctrine that rulers' moral example should replace law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Venizelos explicitly appealed to the nation's right to self-determination and the Allies' defence of small nations.

force-without-un.rationale: Greece went to war in Anatolia on its own after the Allies stalled; the UN did not exist, so inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kolettis invoked faith and religion as the national bond, not reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Anachronistic for the period; the idea had no welfare-eligibility position.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Anachronistic; the kingdom and the idea had no welfare system to condition.

class-collaboration.rationale: Venizelism sought national unity across classes and treated nationalism as superior to class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The idea draws legitimacy from classical and Byzantine heritage that Kolettis celebrates.

dominated-front.rationale: The idea instead sought alignment with the Western powers and Britain, so no common front.

workers-nation.rationale: The idea treated workers as part of the Greek nation, rejecting class internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the social conservatism of the period.

ban-interest.rationale: Not an Orthodox-Greek national position; inferred from a capitalist liberal outlook.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Greek claims were framed around nation and religion, not racial segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state was seen as a national instrument, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic to a 19th and early 20th-century irredentist idea.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalist state-building favoured homogenising citizens, and Venizelos wanted remaining states to be nationally uniform; inferred for immigrants.

elite-replacement.rationale: No such conspiracy theory belongs to the idea.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not part of the idea; no position is documented.

national-mission.rationale: Kolettis frames Greece as a successor to Athens that enlightened others and restoring a Byzantine centre, a civilising role, though not through imposing a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from traditional gender order of the time.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Kolettis's era was marked by patronage and Venizelists attacked royalist politicians, but it is not the idea's content.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Anachronistic; Orthodox identity would reject it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the army's central role.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The idea requires an active, expansionist and military state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Kolettis defined Greekness by religion and allegiance rather than blood.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kolettis argued that all Greeks, born inside or outside the kingdom, should have equal civil rights, though the claim was limited to the Hellenic nation.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialist strategy is unrelated to the idea.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Greek claims relied on historical presence.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religion-based civil law was Ottoman practice, but the idea took no stated stand on a uniform code.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Orthodox identity was national, but no law restricting conversion is documented as part of the idea.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Orthodox education was integral to Greek national schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The statement concerns a socialist state, which does not apply to the idea.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Venizelos grounded claims in the self-determination of populations and Kolettis in the oath and participation of the Greek people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance was not part of the idea's programme.

population-transfer.rationale: Venizelos proposed reciprocal migrations to make Turkey nearly entirely Muslim and later led the compulsory 1923 exchange.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Irredentist war was an accepted instrument.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The sources give no claim that struggle between peoples drives progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No source records a view on outlawing anti-constitutional parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-Ottoman struggle was against servitude, but the statement concerns republican theory.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutionalism was central to 1844 and 1911 politics, so separation of powers is plausible but not a stated aim.

vanguard-party.rationale: Opposed to a revolutionary-class party doctrine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The idea did not prioritise the poor; its focus was national unification.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is anachronistic to the idea.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour-law detail was outside the idea and adherents shared no line.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The idea has no theory of the causes of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Venizelos wanted homogeneity in the post-war settlement, inferred as a preference for ethnic and religious uniformity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not part of modern Greek constitutional practice.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls were not part of the programme and adherents were not united on them.

party-controls-media.rationale: Venizelism was a parliamentary liberal movement.

party-commands-army.rationale: Greek civil politics saw army under the crown and state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Kolettis wanted citizenship for Greeks born abroad quickly; the question concerns foreign immigrants.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No source links the idea to the pay of representatives.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline was not part of the idea; Greek parties were personal followings.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Greek nationalists sought a sovereign enlarged state, not supranational union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The crown commanded the army, and the monarchy-versus-Venizelist split concerned who controlled it; split.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The idea ties national identity to the Great Church of Constantinople and the episcopal Orthodox hierarchy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Kolettis honoured the metropolitans of 1821 but the state was a constitutional kingdom, not clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The idea is nationalist and mobilised its adherents for war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship for virtue is not documented as part of the idea.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term limits were irrelevant to a monarchy-era idea.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials was not part of the idea.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Greece pursued alliance with the Entente to realise its aims.

people-in-arms.rationale: Venizelos built a professional conscript army, not an armed militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources show no preference for rural over urban life; the idea centred on Athens and Constantinople.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Gathering Greeks divided between Greece and the Ottoman Empire is the central aim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Hellenic education was prized in Kolettis's speech.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Kolettis assigned Greece a civilising role as heir to Athens and Byzantium.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment was not an issue in the idea and adherents had no shared line.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from conservative Orthodox setting.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic debate for the idea, which has no stated view on evolution teaching.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Censorship of pornography was not a theme of the idea.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Kolettis argued that those of Greek descent and 1821 fighters born abroad were entitled to citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Venizelos aimed at national homogeneity; inferred as little support for minority-language rights.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The idea has no stated position on conformity and individuality.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Greece itself was a debtor state, but the idea took no stand on cancelling poor countries' debts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Independence meant territorial union; economic transformation was not central.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1843 revolution forced an elected National Assembly, whose constitution Kolettis debated, and Venizelos revised the constitution in 1911.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The idea sought territory, not rapid economic growth, so it has no stated stance.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are anachronistic to the idea.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; the idea predates nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Monarchy vs republic split; no clear position.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions were not part of the idea.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Claims on historically Greek land were not traded away; the idea sought land, not to cede it, though Venizelos accepted compromise in 1930.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The idea took no doctrinal stand on the justification of property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet debate is unrelated to the idea.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed by the 19th-century Greek national project; adherents have no common line.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred: Greek governments pursued the programme through great-power and Entente alliances, though collective defence was not formulated.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: the idea held that Greek lands taken without Greek consent should be redeemed, which applies the same logic to annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Adherents split: Orthodoxy was central to the idea, yet the Greek state kept the church under civil control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Adherents split: the crown versus Venizelos conflict in the National Schism showed no agreed role for the head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred: the project was one of nation-state building by force of arms, so keeping national territory by force fits.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; Venizelos proposed self-determination and local arrangements in some regions, but the aim was union in one state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: Kolettis and Venizelos worked within a constitutional monarchy, not a sacred one, despite Byzantine memory.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the programme; adherents had no common line.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed by the programme; adherents split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: the 1844 constitution that Kolettis defended and the 1911 Venizelist revision set rulers under constitutional law.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic: the programme predates the space age; no inference is possible.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: the 1844 constitution blended crown, senate and elected chamber, though the idea does not address constitutional design.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred: Greek parliamentary constitutionalism treated leaders as officeholders, though Venizelos drew mass devotion.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anachronistic: no relevant position is documented; adherents split.

missingStatements.text: Greeks and other Christians living under foreign rule should be liberated and joined to their own national state.
missingStatements.rationale: Kolettis called on the deputies to remember the freedom owed to all Christians and Hellenes outside the kingdom, the core of the idea.

missingStatements.text: Constantinople should be the capital of a state that unites its nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Kolettis named Constantinople the great capital and hope of Hellenism; the idea aimed at a state centred there.
missingStatements.declined: Too specific to one city and one national project; other ideologies cannot take a side on it.

notes: Venizelist and royalist adherents differed on monarchy, war aims in 1914-17 and the Asia Minor campaign; Kolettis defined Greeks by Orthodox faith while Venizelos argued from population majorities. Many economic and social answers are inferred.
